findings.title: Admin member routes put :id in params but controllers expect :group_id
findings.body: The new routes `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` and `put "members" => "groups#add_members"` are declared inside `resources :groups, constraints: AdminConstraint.new do ... end`. With that placement Rails treats them as member actions, so the URLs are `DELETE /admin/groups/:id/members` and `PUT /admin/groups/:id/members` and the group id is exposed as `params[:id]`. However, `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` (line 66) and `#remove_member` (line 85) both call `params.require(:group_id).to_i`, and the routes never populate `params[:group_id]`. Every AJAX call from the new admin UI to add or remove a member will therefore raise `ActionController::ParameterMissing: param not found: group_id` and return a 400 error, so the new add/remove member functionality does not work. The controller specs pass because `xhr :put/:delete, :add_members/:remove_member, group_id: ...` bypasses routing and injects `group_id` directly into params. Fix by changing the controllers to read `params[:id]`, or by wrapping the routes in `member do ... end`, or by naming the resource param explicitly (e.g. `param: :group_id`).

findings.title: totalPages formula overcounts when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
findings.body: The `totalPages` computed property returns `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. For `user_count = 50` and `limit = 50` this yields `1 + 1 = 2`, but there is only a single page of members. As a result `showingLast` is `false` while the admin is on the only existing page, so the "next" anchor stays enabled. Clicking it sets `offset = user_count` and triggers `findMembers`, which then requests a page that returns `members: []`. The page indicator shows "1/2" with no members and the admin must click "previous" to see them. The correct formula is `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`.

findings.title: add_members does not strip whitespace, so usernames with surrounding spaces are silently dropped
findings.body: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, `usernames.split(",").each do |username|` does not strip whitespace before calling `User.find_by_username(username)`. If the admin types "alice, bob" (note the space after the comma) or pastes a comma-separated list with spaces or line breaks, `User.find_by_username(" bob")` returns nil and that user is silently skipped. The endpoint still returns `success_json`, so the admin sees a green success state even when only some (or none) of the listed users were added, with no indication that anything was missed. Strip whitespace (and skip blank entries) before the lookup, e.g. `username.strip` and `next if username.empty?`.

findings.title: remove_member deletes the join record before group.save, leaving validation errors in an inconsistent state
findings.body: `group.users.delete(user_id)` on a `has_many :through` association deletes the join record from the database immediately. The subsequent `group.save` only persists Group-model attribute changes, not the membership change. If Group validation fails (e.g. a uniqueness validator on `name`), the controller responds with `render_json_error(group)`, but the membership removal has already been committed. The client therefore sees an error response while the member has actually been removed from the group. Either drop the `group.save` (the membership change already succeeded) or perform the deletion and the save inside a single transaction so they commit or fail together.
